key_insight: Scaling the feed-forward VGGT architecture to VGGT-Ω yields predictable, monotonic improvements in reconstruction quality with increased model and data size, while also boosting efficiency and enabling robust handling of both static and dynamic scenes.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between optimization-based 3D reconstructors and fast feed-forward models by improving accuracy, efficiency, and generalization to dynamic scenes, while providing geometry-aware features useful for downstream tasks.
method: Introduce VGGT-Ω: a scaled-up, feed-forward reconstruction architecture that leverages increased model capacity and larger training datasets to improve geometric fidelity.
Engineering and training pipeline optimizations to enable training at unprecedented scale (efficient data pipelines, distributed training, and scaling-aware regularization).
Design and loss components to support both static and dynamic scene reconstruction and to produce geometry-aware feature representations for downstream use.
impact: Practitioners get a fast, scalable reconstructor that approaches or surpasses traditional optimization methods in accuracy while being orders of magnitude faster and offering reusable geometry-aware features—allowing predictable trade-offs when allocating model and data budgets.
visual_elements: Scaling law chart: model size / dataset size on x-axis vs reconstruction accuracy on y-axis to show predictable improvement.
Side-by-side qualitative comparisons: ground truth, baseline VGGT, and VGGT-Ω reconstructions for both static and dynamic scenes.
Architecture diagram: high-level feed-forward pipeline of VGGT-Ω highlighting geometry-aware feature extraction and efficient inference.
Performance bar chart: inference time and memory vs optimization-based reconstructor and prior VGGT versions.
paper_authors: Jianyuan Wang, Minghao Chen, Shangzhan Zhang, Nikita Karaev, Johannes Schönberger
